properties.label: Young's modulus
properties.definition: Slope of the uniaxial elastic stress-strain response.

properties.label: Flexural modulus
properties.definition: Modulus measured in bending, including the source test geometry and shear contribution. Kept separate from tensile Young's modulus.

properties.label: Ultimate tensile strength
properties.definition: Maximum engineering tensile stress reached in a tensile test.

properties.label: Tensile yield strength
properties.definition: Stress at the specified onset of permanent tensile deformation. Basis and conditioned product geometry must be compared like-for-like.

properties.label: Flexural strength
properties.definition: Stress at failure in the cited bending test; distinguish from tensile strength.

properties.label: Compressive strength
properties.definition: Stress at failure in the cited compression test. Specimen shape and age change the result, so read the stated method.

properties.label: Thermal conductivity
properties.definition: Proportionality between conductive heat flux and temperature gradient.

properties.label: Specific heat capacity
properties.definition: Energy per unit mass and temperature change, at the reported temperature.

properties.label: Poisson’s ratio
properties.definition: Ratio of transverse contraction to axial extension in elastic loading.

properties.label: Elongation at break
properties.definition: Engineering strain at fracture, stored as a fraction rather than percent.

indices.name: Heat spreading per unit mass
indices.scope: Lightweight heat spreaders, mass-limited thermal management.
indices.source: Ashby, M. F. (2011). Materials Selection in Mechanical Design, 4th ed. §11.7.
indices.derivation: For lightweight heat spreaders (e.g. aerospace electronics), maximizing thermal conductivity per unit mass gives M = k/ρ.

indices.name: Max elastic stored energy / volume
indices.source: Ashby, M. F. (2011). Materials Selection in Mechanical Design, 4th ed. Ch. 5–6.
indices.derivation: The elastic energy stored per unit volume before yield is σ_y²/(2E).  Maximizing this gives M = σ_y²/E.

indices.name: Stiff, light beam
indices.scope: Fixed length, bending stiffness constraint, free cross-section.
indices.source: Ashby, M. F. (2011). Materials Selection in Mechanical Design, 4th ed. Ch. 5–6.
indices.derivation: For a beam of fixed length and prescribed bending stiffness, minimizing mass yields M = E^(1/2)/ρ.  The cross-section is a free variable (can be resized).

indices.name: Stiff, light plate
indices.scope: Fixed area, bending stiffness constraint (plate geometry).
indices.source: Ashby, M. F. (2011). Materials Selection in Mechanical Design, 4th ed. Ch. 5–6.
indices.derivation: For a plate of fixed area loaded in bending, minimizing mass at constant stiffness yields M = E^(1/3)/ρ.  Thickness is the free variable.

indices.name: Stiff, light tie
indices.source: Ashby, M. F. (2011). Materials Selection in Mechanical Design, 4th ed. Ch. 5–6.
indices.derivation: For an axially loaded tie of fixed length, minimizing mass at constant axial stiffness yields M = E/ρ.  Derived from F/δ = EA/L with m = ρAL. F: axial force; δ: extension; A: area; L: length; m: mass.

indices.name: Strong, light beam
indices.scope: Fixed length, bending strength, free cross-section.
indices.source: Ashby, M. F. (2011). Materials Selection in Mechanical Design, 4th ed. Ch. 5–6.
indices.derivation: For a beam of fixed length that must not yield in bending, minimizing mass with free cross-section yields M = σ_y^(2/3)/ρ.

indices.name: Strong, light plate
indices.source: Ashby, M. F. (2011). Materials Selection in Mechanical Design, 4th ed. Ch. 5–6.
indices.derivation: For a plate of fixed area that must not yield in bending, minimizing mass with free thickness yields M = σ_y^(1/2)/ρ.

indices.name: Strong, light tie
indices.scope: Fixed length, yield strength in tension.
indices.source: Ashby, M. F. (2011). Materials Selection in Mechanical Design, 4th ed. Ch. 5–6.
indices.derivation: For a tie of fixed length that must not yield under axial load, minimizing mass yields M = σ_y/ρ.

indices.name: Thermal insulation
indices.source: Ashby, M. F. (2011). Materials Selection in Mechanical Design, 4th ed. §11.7.
indices.derivation: Minimizing steady-state heat flow through a wall of fixed thickness requires minimizing thermal conductivity.

indices.name: Volumetric thermal storage
indices.scope: Thermal mass, passive thermal storage.  NOT heat sink performance (which depends on k and convection geometry).
indices.source: Ashby, M. F. (2011). Materials Selection in Mechanical Design, 4th ed. §11.7.
indices.derivation: The energy stored per unit volume for a given ΔT is ρ·Cₚ·ΔT.  Maximizing ρ·Cₚ maximizes volumetric thermal storage. ΔT: temperature change.
